note: Continuous timeline: sequence numbers run 1-11 for FREN151 (weeks 1-11) then 11-23 for FREN152 (weeks 2-13, since FREN152's own week 1 has no separate tutorial content).

topics.title: Gender & articles (un/une/des, le/la/les/l')
topics.rule: Nouns are masculine or feminine. A: un (m) / une (f) / des (pl). THE: le (m) / la (f) / les (pl); both le and la become l' before a vowel or silent h.

items.en: How do you say ... in French?

items.fr: Vous pouvez réexpliquer, s'il vous plaît?
items.en: Can you explain that again please?

bonus_sentences.fr: Bonjour, je m'appelle Léa.
bonus_sentences.en: Hello, my name is Léa.

items.en: see you / see you next time

topics.title: Regular verb conjugation groups
topics.rule: French has three groups of regular verbs, named after their infinitive endings: -er, -ir, -re.

topics.title: -er verb conjugation (parler)
topics.rule: Remove -ER from the infinitive to get the stem, then add: -e, -es, -e, -ons, -ez, -ent.

topics.title: Asking someone's nationality

items.en: I am an Australian of Lebanese extraction.

topics.rule: Feminine nationality usually adds -e (unless already ending in e); nationalities ending in -ien add -enne. Plural: add -s (masc./mixed) or -es (fem.); already-s endings don't double.

bonus_sentences.fr: Je parle français et j'habite à Lyon.
bonus_sentences.en: I speak French and I live in Lyon.

topics.title: Elision and liaison
topics.rule: Elision: a final vowel is dropped and replaced with an apostrophe before a word starting with a vowel or silent h (je, le, la, de, que, ne, se, ce, si). Liaison: a normally-silent final consonant is pronounced when the next word starts with a vowel.

topics.title: Reflexive (pronominal) verbs
topics.rule: Reflexive verbs take a reflexive pronoun immediately before the verb, matching the subject.

bonus_sentences.fr: J'ai besoin d'un livre et d'un smartphone.
bonus_sentences.en: I need a book and a smartphone.

topics.title: Uses of 'pour'

items.en: I am studying French to travel

topics.rule: 'Pour' translates 'for', or 'in order to' when followed by an infinitive.

items.fr: agent de police / agente de police

topics.title: Asking someone's occupation

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que tu fais dans la vie?
items.en: What do you do for a living? (informal)

items.fr: Qu'est-ce que vous faites dans la vie?
items.en: What do you do for a living? (formal)

topics.rule: No article (un/une) before an occupation after 'être' or 'travailler comme' — e.g. 'Je suis professeur', not 'Je suis un professeur'. But an article IS used after 'c'est': 'C'est une actrice'.

items.fr: Je travaille à temps plein / complet.

topics.title: University subjects (les matières)
topics.rule: J'ai un cours de/un examen de + [subject] = I have a class/exam in... 'Devoir + infinitive' expresses what subject someone must study (Il doit étudier la médecine).

bonus_sentences.fr: Je travaille comme cuisinier pour voyager.
bonus_sentences.en: I work as a cook to travel.

topics.title: 'From' and 'to' with countries
topics.rule: Countries ending in -e are almost always feminine; others are masculine. de/d' (fem.), du (masc.), des (plural) = 'from'. en (fem.), au (masc.), aux (plural) = 'to/in'. Towns/cities use de and à regardless of gender.

topics.title: Aller (to go) and Venir (to come)
topics.rule: Aller and venir are irregular and must be memorised.

topics.title: Numbers 60-100
topics.rule: French counts 70-99 in base-20 style: soixante-dix (60+10), quatre-vingts (4x20), quatre-vingt-dix (4x20+10).

items.fr: Quel est ton/votre numéro de téléphone?
accepted_fr: Quel est ton/votre numéro de téléphone?
Quel est ton numéro de téléphone?
Quel est votre numéro de téléphone?

topics.title: The negative (ne...pas)

items.en: I don't have a tablet. (un/une/des → de after negative)
It isn't a smartphone. (être keeps un/une)

topics.rule: 'ne' and 'pas' surround the conjugated verb. After ne...pas, un/une/des become just 'de' — except with the verb être.

items.fr: Est-ce que tu as un ordinateur?

topics.title: Belgian/Swiss number variants
topics.rule: These regional number words replace the standard French 70/80/90 forms entirely in Belgian and Swiss French — not additional options, but different words for the same number.

bonus_sentences.fr: Je viens d'Australie et je vais en France.
bonus_sentences.en: I come from Australia and I am going to France.

items.fr: Pour aller à (au/à la/aux/à l')..., s'il vous plaît?
items.en: How do I get to..., please?

accepted_en: Is there a... close to here?
accepted_fr: Est-ce qu'il y a... près d'ici?

topics.title: Vivre (to live)
topics.rule: Habiter is used only for the place/building you live in. Vivre is broader: place, 'to be alive', 'to live through', manner of living.

topics.title: Places in a town II (water, worship, streets)
Giving an opinion on a city

bonus_sentences.fr: Tournez à droite, puis continuez tout droit.
bonus_sentences.en: Turn right, then carry on straight ahead.

topics.title: il y a / il n'y a pas de

items.fr: Il n'y a pas de théâtre.

topics.rule: Il y a + un/une/des for affirmative; il n'y a pas de/d' for negative (article dropped).

topics.title: Prepositions of place

items.fr: à côté du / de la / de l' / des

topics.rule: Longer prepositions ending in 'de' combine with the definite article: de+le→du, de+les→des, de+la/l' stay the same.

topics.title: Expressions of quantity
topics.rule: After an expression of quantity, no article is used — just the plural noun (quelques églises, beaucoup de magasins). Exceptions: un hôpital→des hôpitaux, un centre commercial→des centres commerciaux keep irregular plurals.

bonus_sentences.fr: Il y a beaucoup de restaurants en face du parc.
bonus_sentences.en: There are many restaurants opposite the park.

topics.title: Position of adjectives (BAGS)
topics.rule: Most adjectives come AFTER the noun (un quartier dynamique). BAGS adjectives (Beauty, Age, Goodness, Size) come BEFORE the noun instead (une belle ville, un petit parc).

topics.title: Adverbs modifying adjectives
topics.rule: Adverbs like assez/très are placed before the adjective they modify: c'est un quartier assez agréable.

topics.title: Elision rule (recap)
topics.rule: Elision (je, me, te, se, le, la, ce, ne, de, que, si) drops the final vowel before a word starting with a vowel or silent h.

topics.title: Nationalities & capitalisation

items.en: I speak French and German. (lowercase language)
The Germans are hard-working. (capitalised noun for people)
accepted_en: The Germans are hard-working. (capitalised noun for people)

topics.rule: Nationality adjectives and language names are lowercase in French; nouns referring to the people of a nation are capitalised.

topics.title: à/de + definite article contractions
topics.rule: à+la and à+l', de+la and de+l' do NOT contract — only le and les contract.

items.en: I am a student. (no article before occupation)
I like tennis. (definite article after like/dislike verbs)
I don't have a car. (un/une/des → de after negation)
It isn't a Hyundai. (être keeps un/une in the negative)

topics.title: Verb placement rules

items.en: I like to swim. (2nd verb stays infinitive)

items.fr: Je n'aime pas faire de l'équitation.
items.en: I don't like horse-riding. (ne...pas surrounds the FIRST verb)
accepted_en: I don't like horse-riding. (ne...pas surrounds the FIRST verb)

topics.rule: With two verbs in a row, only the first is conjugated; the second stays in the infinitive. Negation wraps the first (conjugated) verb only.

topics.title: aussi (also/too) placement

items.fr: J'adore nager, j'aime aussi faire du surf.
items.en: I love swimming, I also like surfing.

topics.rule: 'Aussi' meaning 'also/too' goes AFTER the verb, never at the start of a sentence (starting with aussi changes its meaning to 'therefore').

items.en: The book is good. (bon/bonne describes a noun)

bonus_sentences.fr: C'est un très vieux quartier, animé et multiculturel.
bonus_sentences.en: It's a very old neighbourhood, lively and multicultural.

items.fr: le frère cadet / la sœur cadette
le frère aîné / la sœur aînée

topics.title: Possessive adjectives
topics.rule: Possessive adjectives agree with the noun they precede, not the owner's gender. Mon/ton/son are also used before feminine words starting with a vowel sound (mon amie).

items.fr: Combien de personnes y a-t-il dans ta famille?
items.en: How many people are in your family?

items.fr: As-tu des frères ou des sœurs?
items.en: Do you have brothers or sisters?

topics.title: Possessive with 'de' (Elizabeth's boyfriend)
topics.rule: French has no 's; use [thing] + de + [owner]. 'De' contracts with le/les into du/des.

topics.title: Verbs of like/dislike + infinitive
topics.rule: Verbs of like/dislike are followed by an infinitive (j'aime nager) or, if a noun, the definite article (j'aime le tennis). préférer has an accent change (è vs é) but regular endings.

bonus_sentences.fr: Mon frère aime faire du vélo avec ses amis.
bonus_sentences.en: My brother likes to go biking with his friends.

topics.title: C'est vs Il est/Elle est

items.en: That's Nathalie. / That's a Peugeot. (c'est + proper noun)

items.fr: C'est une amie. / C'est une bonne étudiante.
items.en: She's a friend. / She's a good student. (c'est + article + noun)

items.fr: Elle est sympathique. / Elle est rapide.
items.en: She's nice. / It's fast. (il/elle est + adjective ONLY, no article)

items.fr: Mon frère, il est à Paris.
items.en: My brother is in Paris. (il/elle est + preposition, for location)
accepted_fr: Mon frère, il est à Paris.
Mon frère, il est à Paris
Mon frère il est à Paris

items.fr: Ce n'est pas Élodie. / Ce sont des crayons. / Ce ne sont pas des stylos.
items.en: That's not Élodie. / Those are pencils. / Those aren't pens. (negative & plural forms)

topics.rule: Elle/il can mean 'she/he' (person) OR 'it' (referring to a feminine/masculine noun already mentioned, e.g. la voiture → elle). For occupations, either form works: Il est professeur (no article) or C'est un professeur (with article) — but never 'Il est un professeur.'

topics.title: Irregular adjective patterns
topics.rule: Related noun pattern follows the same logic: un champion→une championne, un acteur→une actrice, un journal→des journaux, un animal→des animaux. The -al→-aux irregularity affects masculine plural only.

bonus_sentences.fr: J'aime beaucoup le tennis, mais je n'aime pas trop le ski.
bonus_sentences.en: I like tennis a lot, but I don't like skiing too much.

topics.title: Physical attributes
topics.rule: The definite article (les) is required before 'hair' and 'eyes' in French, unlike in English.

topics.title: Regular adjective agreement

items.fr: drôle (masc./fem. sg, ends in silent e)

topics.rule: Regular adjectives: masc. sg = base form; fem. sg = base+e; masc. pl = base+s; fem. pl = base+es. Adjectives already ending in silent -e don't add another e in the feminine.

topics.title: Il est / Elle est vs C'est

items.en: He's a teacher. (il est + occupation, no article)

items.fr: Mon frère, il est à Paris.
items.en: My brother is in Paris. (il/elle est + preposition for place)

topics.rule: C'est + noun; Il/Elle est + adjective, occupation (no article), or place preposition. Il/elle can also mean 'it' when referring back to an object.

bonus_sentences.fr: Elle est sportive et elle a les cheveux longs.
bonus_sentences.en: She is sporty and she has long hair.

topics.title: Telling the time

items.fr: Il est cinq heures moins vingt de l'après-midi.
accepted_en: It's twenty to five in the afternoon

topics.rule: French can express time two ways: 12hr clock with du matin/de l'après-midi/du soir, or the 24hr clock (more common in writing/timetables).

topics.title: Numbers 60 to a billion
topics.rule: 'Et' is only used in double-digit numbers ending in 1 (21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 71) — never in larger numbers like 301 (trois cent un) or 5023 (cinq mille vingt-trois).

accepted_fr: mille neuf cent quatre vingt douze
accepted_en: one thousand nine hundred and ninety-two

accepted_fr: dix neuf cent quatre vingt douze

topics.title: The present tense: -ir and -re verbs

items.fr: je finis / tu finis / il finit
items.en: I/you/he finish(es) (-ir pattern, e.g. finir, choisir, réussir, grossir, maigrir, réfléchir)
accepted_en: I/you/he finish(es) (-ir pattern, e.g. finir, choisir, réussir, grossir, maigrir, réfléchir)
I finish / you finish / he finishes
I finish, you finish, he finishes

items.fr: nous finissons / vous finissez / ils finissent
accepted_en: we finish / you finish / they finish
we finish, you finish, they finish

items.fr: je vends / tu vends / il vend
items.en: I/you/he sell(s) (-re pattern, e.g. vendre, attendre, répondre, rendre, perdre)
accepted_en: I/you/he sell(s) (-re pattern, e.g. vendre, attendre, répondre, rendre, perdre)
I sell / you sell / he sells
I sell, you sell, he sells

items.fr: nous vendons / vous vendez / ils vendent
accepted_en: we sell / you sell / they sell
we sell, you sell, they sell

topics.rule: -ir verbs (like finir): stem + is, is, it, issons, issez, issent. -re verbs (like vendre): stem + s, s, [nothing], ons, ez, ent.

topics.title: Time words: quarters, halves and minutes
topics.rule: On the 12-hour clock the minutes after the half hour are counted backwards with moins (moins vingt, moins le quart). The 24-hour clock just counts forward (quarante, quarante-cinq). Midi and minuit never need du matin or du soir.

items.fr: Il est trois heures et demie.
Il est dix heures moins le quart.
accepted_en: It is a quarter to ten

items.en: It is a quarter past midnight.
accepted_en: It is a quarter past midnight.
It is half past three in the afternoon

items.fr: Il est vingt et une heures quarante-cinq.
accepted_en: It is a quarter to ten in the evening

topics.title: Asking and saying when something happens

items.fr: À quelle heure est le cours?
accepted_en: At what time is the class
At what time is the lesson

items.fr: Le cours est à dix heures.
items.en: The class is at ten o'clock.
accepted_en: The class is at ten o'clock.
The lesson is at ten o'clock

items.fr: De neuf heures à dix heures.
À quelle heure finit le cours?
items.en: What time does the class end?
accepted_en: What time does the class end?
What time does the lesson end
At what time does the class end
What time does the class finish
What time does the lesson finish

items.fr: Il est une heure du matin.
items.en: It is one o'clock in the morning.
accepted_en: It is one o'clock in the morning.
It is one in the morning

topics.title: Plurals in big numbers
topics.rule: Vingt and cent take an s only when multiplied and nothing follows (quatre-vingts, deux cents). Mille never takes an s. Million and milliard do, and are followed by de before a noun.

bonus_sentences.fr: Je finis à midi et je vends des livres.
bonus_sentences.en: I finish at noon and I sell books.

topics.title: Days of the week
topics.rule: Days of the week are NOT capitalised in French, unlike English.

items.en: on Mondays (habitually; lundi = on one particular Monday)
accepted_en: on Mondays (habitually; lundi = on one particular Monday)

items.fr: le matin / le midi / l'après-midi / le soir
items.en: in the mornings/at noon/in the afternoons/in the evenings (habitually)
accepted_en: in the mornings/at noon/in the afternoons/in the evenings (habitually)

topics.title: jouer à / jouer de / faire de

items.fr: jouer au rugby / au tennis / aux échecs
jouer du piano / de la guitare
faire du vélo / de la natation
items.en: to do cycling/swimming (general activities take 'faire de')
accepted_en: to do cycling/swimming (general activities take 'faire de')

topics.rule: jouer à + le/la/les/l' → au/à la/aux/à l' for sports and games. jouer de + le/la/les/l' → du/de la/des/de l' for musical instruments.

topics.title: Adverbs and phrases of frequency
topics.rule: One-word adverbs (jamais, souvent, toujours, etc.) go after the verb (Je vais toujours en cours); in the negative, after 'pas' (Je ne vais pas toujours...). Multi-word adverbial phrases (une fois par semaine, etc.) can go at the start or end of the sentence.

topics.title: Reflexive verbs in the present (se laver)
topics.rule: A reflexive verb takes a pronoun that matches the subject: me, te, se, nous, vous, se, placed before the verb. In the infinitive the pronoun is se (se laver). Nous and vous use the same word as the subject pronoun.

topics.title: Reflexive verbs with a stem change (se lever)
topics.rule: Se lever takes a grave accent (è) where the ending is silent: je, tu, il and ils. Nous and vous keep a plain e. Se promener works the same way (je me promène, nous nous promenons).

topics.title: Reflexive verbs before a vowel (s'habiller)
topics.rule: Me, te and se shorten to m', t' and s' before a vowel or a silent h (je m'habille, il s'endort). Nous and vous never shorten.

topics.title: Reflexive verbs and parts of the body
topics.rule: With a reflexive verb and a part of the body French uses the (les, la, le), not my or his: the reflexive pronoun already says whose it is.

topics.title: Never: ne ... jamais

items.fr: Je ne fais jamais de ski.
Elle ne se lève jamais tôt.
Tu ne regardes jamais la télé?

topics.rule: Ne and jamais wrap the verb exactly like ne ... pas. Jamais can also stand alone as a short answer (Jamais!). After ne ... jamais the partitive becomes de (jamais de sport).

items.fr: Je me réveille à sept heures.
accepted_en: I wake up at seven o'clock
I am waking up at seven

items.fr: D'abord, je me douche, ensuite je m'habille.
items.en: First I take a shower, then I get dressed.
accepted_en: First I take a shower, then I get dressed.
First I shower, then I get dressed
First I have a shower, then I get dressed
First I take a shower and then I get dressed

items.fr: Le réveil sonne à six heures.
items.en: The alarm clock rings at six.
accepted_en: The alarm clock rings at six.
The alarm clock goes off at six
The alarm goes off at six

items.fr: Je me couche avant onze heures.
items.en: I go to bed before eleven.
accepted_en: I go to bed before eleven.
I go to bed before eleven o'clock
I go to sleep before eleven

items.fr: Le week-end, je me lève tard.
items.en: At the weekend I get up late.
accepted_en: At the weekend I get up late.
On the weekend I get up late
At weekends I get up late
On weekends I get up late
During the week I hurry up
I have a rest on Sundays

bonus_sentences.fr: Le lundi, je me réveille et je joue au tennis.
bonus_sentences.en: On Mondays, I wake up and I play tennis.

topics.title: Prendre (to take) and Sortir (to go out)

items.fr: je prends / tu prends / il prend
accepted_en: I take / you take / he takes
I take, you take, he takes

items.fr: nous prenons / vous prenez / ils prennent
accepted_en: we take / you take / they take
we take, you take, they take

items.fr: je sors / tu sors / il sort
accepted_en: I go out / you go out / he goes out
I go out, you go out, he goes out

items.fr: nous sortons / vous sortez / ils sortent
accepted_en: we go out / you go out / they go out
we go out, you go out, they go out

topics.rule: Sortir-type verbs (dormir, s'endormir, partir, servir) have two stems: singular forms drop the last 3 letters of the infinitive, plural forms drop only the last 2.

accepted_en: I go out with my friends
I'm going out with my friends
I hang out with my friends

items.fr: je me promène sur la plage
items.en: I go for a walk on the beach
accepted_en: I go for a walk on the beach
I take a walk on the beach
I go for a stroll on the beach
I go walking on the beach
I watch my favourite TV show
I watch my favorite TV show

topics.title: The comparative

items.fr: Jacques est plus grand que Julie.

items.en: better (irregular comparative of bon — 'plus bon' doesn't exist)

topics.rule: que becomes qu' before a vowel. The adjective agrees with the sentence's subject, not the comparison target.

topics.title: The superlative

items.fr: Le sport le plus intéressant, c'est le rugby.
items.en: The most interesting sport is rugby.
best / worst (irregular, come before the noun like BAGS adjectives)

topics.rule: Superlative uses definite article + plus/moins + adjective; 'de' after the superlative translates 'in' (la plus grande ville du monde). meilleur/pire and BAGS-type adjectives (beau, nouveau, vieux, bon, gentil, mauvais, grand, petit, gros, haut, large, bref) go BEFORE the noun even in the superlative.

items.fr: À quelle heure est ton rendez-vous?
accepted_en: At what time is your appointment

items.fr: Mon cours de judo est à dix-sept heures.
accepted_en: My judo class is at five pm
My judo class is at 5 pm
My judo class is at five in the afternoon
My judo class is at five o'clock

items.fr: Mon cours est de dix heures à onze heures.
items.en: My class is from ten to eleven.
accepted_en: My class is from ten to eleven.
My lesson is from ten to eleven
My class is from ten until eleven

items.en: What are you doing on Thursday?
accepted_en: What are you doing on Thursday?
What do you do on Thursday
What are you doing this Thursday

items.en: I am going to the dentist's.
accepted_en: I am going to the dentist's.
I am going to the dentist

items.fr: Je vais à une soirée déguisée.
items.en: I am going to a costume party.
accepted_en: I am going to a costume party.
I'm going to a costume party
I am going to a fancy dress party
I'm going to a fancy dress party
I go to a costume party

items.fr: Je vais au marché ce week-end.
items.en: I am going to the market this weekend.
accepted_en: I am going to the market this weekend.
I'm going to the market this weekend
I am going to the market at the weekend
I'm going to the market at the weekend

topics.title: Jouer à, jouer de or faire de?

items.fr: Mon frère joue de la batterie.

topics.rule: Jouer à + a game or sport (au, à la, aux, à l'). Jouer de + an instrument (du, de la, des, de l'). Faire de + an activity you do rather than play (du vélo, de la natation); team sports can take either jouer à or faire de.

topics.title: Verbs like sortir, and daily habits

bonus_sentences.fr: Léa est plus travailleuse que Marc, et Marc est aussi gourmand que Léa.
bonus_sentences.en: Léa is more hard-working than Marc, and Marc is as greedy as Léa.

topics.title: Dates and birthdays

items.fr: Quelle est la date de ton anniversaire?
accepted_en: What is the date of your birthday?
What's the date of your birthday?

topics.rule: French uses cardinal numbers for dates (le 3 octobre), not ordinal numbers like English's 'the third'.

accepted_en: How many times a day / week / month...?

topics.title: Asking questions: est-ce que and inversion

items.en: Where do you live? (est-ce que form)

items.fr: où / quand / comment / pourquoi / qui / combien / quel(le)
items.en: where / when / how / why / who / how much-many / which-what
accepted_en: where / when / how / why / who / how much-many / which-what

topics.rule: Two main ways to form a question: (1) question word + est-ce que + normal word order, or (2) inversion of the verb and subject pronoun (more formal/written).

topics.title: '-t-' insertion in inverted questions

items.en: Does he work? (verb ends in vowel sound — needs inserted -t-)
accepted_en: Does he work? (verb ends in vowel sound — needs inserted -t-)

items.en: Does he take? (verb already ends in -d, pronounced 't' — no insertion needed)
accepted_en: Does he take? (verb already ends in -d, pronounced 't' — no insertion needed)

items.en: Does he finish? (verb already ends in -t — no insertion needed)
accepted_en: Does he finish? (verb already ends in -t — no insertion needed)

topics.rule: When inverting a verb and il/elle/on, insert '-t-' between them UNLESS the verb already ends in -d or -t (both pronounced as a 't' sound) — this avoids an awkward vowel clash between two vowel sounds.

items.en: It is the first of April.
accepted_en: It is the first of April.

items.en: It is Saturday the twenty-fifth of July.
accepted_en: It is Saturday the twenty-fifth of July.
It's Saturday the twenty-fifth of July
It is Saturday the 25th of July

items.fr: Mon anniversaire est le douze mai.
items.en: My birthday is on the twelfth of May.
accepted_en: My birthday is on the twelfth of May.
My birthday is the twelfth of May
My birthday is the 12th of May
My birthday is on the 12th of May

topics.title: The first of the month
topics.rule: Only the first of the month is an ordinal number (le premier). Every other date is an ordinary number: le deux, le quinze, le trente. Days and months have no capital letter in French.

topics.title: Questions in other ways

items.en: What do you do for a living? (formal)
accepted_en: What do you do for a living? (formal)
What do you do for a living

topics.title: The passé composé — regular verbs with avoir
topics.rule: Regular passé composé = present tense of avoir + past participle. -er verbs: -é; -ir verbs: -i; -re verbs: -u. Used for completed past actions or a change of state.

topics.title: The passé composé — adverbs as time markers
topics.rule: Short common adverbs (déjà, bien, souvent, trop, vraiment...) go between avoir and the past participle. Longer adverbs of manner tend to follow the past participle. Time expressions often go at the start or end of the sentence.

topics.rule: Around 14 verbs of movement/state (mnemonic: MRS VAN DER TRAMP) take être instead of avoir in the passé composé, and the past participle agrees in gender/number with the subject (elle est allée, ils sont partis).

topics.title: Reflexive verbs in the passé composé
topics.rule: Reflexive verbs always take être in the passé composé, with the past participle agreeing with the subject — UNLESS a direct object noun follows the verb (elle s'est lavé les mains — no agreement, because 'les mains' is the direct object, not the reflexive pronoun).

topics.title: Disjunctive (emphatic) pronouns
topics.rule: Used to emphasise a subject (Moi, je parle français), before/after et or ou joining people, in short answers with no verb (Qui parle français? — Moi!), after c'est/ce n'est pas, and after most prepositions (avec elle, pour lui).
